newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina sees Amsterdam listing for Sigm.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina sees Amsterdam listing for Sigm.

text.p: Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina said on Monday it could seek a stock market listing in the next few years for its 100-percent owned Dutch paints unit Sigma Coatings Holding BV.

"In the longer-term it's our intention to give freedom to the Sigma group by giving them their own quotation on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange," PetroFina chief executive officer Francois Cornelis told a news conference ahead of the group's annual shareholders meeting.
He gave no timescale for a listing and said it was too early to discuss details, such as the size of Sigma's free float.
In the short term, Sigma had its own growth plans which would contribute to the PetroFina group, Cornelis said. After a flat 1996, Sigma should be more profitable in 1997, he said.
"In order to do (a listing) we want to build up strength. That's what we are doing at the moment," Cornelis added.

Cornelis declined to place a value on Sigma. According to PetroFina's annual report, paint sales rose to 29.6 billion francs in 1996 from 28.7 billion a year earlier. Operating profit was 1.1 billion francs, down from 1.3 billion.
Cornelis suggested in a newspaper interview last year that Sigma could one day be spun off, but gave no details.
